identity.title: Does transcutaneous electric acupoint stimulation improve the quality of recovery after thyroidectomy? A prospective randomized controlled trial
identity.notes: Yanqing Chen, Yang Yang, Yusheng Yao, Dongsheng Dai, Bin Qian, Pingping Liu; IJCEM8(8):13622–13627, PMID26550304, IJCEM0010937; publishedAugust30,2015.

registration.finding: Current record specifies primary globalQoR40 at24h; secondaryPONV,pain,satisfaction. Rescue counts and PACU duration are not listed in current outcomes. No dated SAP or earliest registry-version content verified; chronology within enrollment month is uncertain.

design.population: Women18–60,ASA I–II, elective thyroidectomy under GA; Fujian Provincial Hospital January–May2015.
design.comparator: Sham / no-current electrodes at same acupoints
design.intervention: BilateralLI4/PC6,2/10Hz,6–9mA adjusted to slight muscle twitch/maximum tolerance,30min awake before induction.
design.randomization: Computer-generated table; sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes.
design.blinding: Claims patients, attending anesthesiologist, surgeons and collector blinded, but awake perceptible stimulation contrasts with inactive sham; no blinding-success assessment.
design.attrition: One TEAS patient discontinued for unspecified protocol breach;83/84 analyzed.

regimen.pca: No PCA reported; standardized2mg IV morphine rescue boluses when VAS needs reduction below4.
regimen.rescue: IV morphine2mg per rescue to maintainVAS<4; no other postoperative opioid regimen reported.
regimen.anesthesia: Sufentanil0.5µg/kg and propofol2mg/kg induction; sevoflurane maintenance; tropisetron5mg before end.

independent_outcomes.conflict: Narrative p4 gives control upper quartile186, whereas table's explicit cell is183. Preserve both as source conflict; table chosen provisionally, not as independent numerical truth from repeated agreement.
EA pain-domainQ3=36 is impossible for seven five-point items(max35) under instrument definitionp2. Do not repair; ask whether domain/global scores were calculated correctly.

independent_outcomes.window: Within first24h; repeated1/2/4/8/24h assessments; averaging rule not explicit
independent_outcomes.conflict: Reported independent t-test P=.013 does not agree with printed mean/SD/n (t about7.35). Preserve raw summaries and printedP; query, not recalculate as replacement.

independent_outcomes.result: Cumulative number of rescue analgesia administrations
independent_outcomes.qualification: Not mg,notmean/SD,notbuttonpresses. Fixed2mg rescue described; no conversion performed and all-systemic coverage not independently confirmed. AbstractP<.001 conflicts with table/proseP=.004.
Not hospital length of stay or QoR.

source_conflicts: AverageVAS mean/SD/n incompatible with printedP=.013 under stated independentt-test
independence: Source-comparison with S063 establishes nonoverlapping enrollment periods (S063Aug–Dec2014;S062Jan–May2015), different ethics approvals(K2014-07-003 vsK2014-12-003), sample sizes and anesthesia/rescue regimens. Same center, PI and TEAS parameters do not imply duplicate patients.

opioid_candidate.reason: Direct24h rescue-administration counts with a documented fixed2mg IV morphine regimen can support a count/median sensitivity result. Not a reported mass mean/SD; no conversion performed. All-systemic coverage needs confirmation.

1.3: No compelling imbalance suggesting failure;83/84 baseline reported. Several printed P values are questionable, but raw demographic contrasts do not establish compromised randomization.
2.1: Awake6–9mA stimulation with muscle twitch versus no current; claimed blinding has no success test.
2.2: Operator necessarily knows whether delivering stimulation.
2.3: One unspecified protocol breach; cannot establish whether caused by trial context.
2.4: Nature of protocol breach not reported; its influence on recovery cannot be assessed.
2.5: Only one TEAS breach reported; no details of corresponding cointerventions or deviations.
2.6: One randomized TEAS participant omitted because of protocol breach.
2.7: Only1/84 omitted; substantial impact on15-point medianQoR contrast or16-event PONV difference is unlikely, though not full ITT.
3.1: 83/84(98.8%) available; essentially all for these sizable contrasts.
4.1: QoR40 is an appropriate validated patient-reported instrument; impossible domain quartile is a reporting/scoring QC problem requiring clarification, not proof of differential measurement.
4.2: Same questionnaire and follow-up timing, blinded collector.
4.3: Participant is the QoR assessor and may discern perceptible preoperative current versus inactive sham.
4.4: Self-reported recovery can be influenced by treatment expectancy.
4.5: No masking-success data or direct evidence of expectancy-related reporting; cannot claim likely influence solely from sensation.
5.1: Registry first postedJan7,2015 within enrollment month; current2016 record is not a dated detailed SAP before unblinding.
5.2: Global24hQoR40 is clearly primary and consistent with current registration; no evidence of selecting a QoR instrument/time based on significance.
5.3: No dated analysis plan establishing median/global/domain handling before access to outcomes.

rob_independent.reason: Good sequence/concealment and near-complete follow-up; unspecified protocol breach, possible sensory unmasking of self-reports and unavailable prospective detailed analysis plan. Source numerical conflicts are separately flagged, not solved by RoB rating.
